issues.legal_issue: A reviewing authority exercising quasi-judicial revision over a mining-lease decision must give reasons for its decision, including when it affirms the original decision.
material_facts: The State Government preferred another applicant for the mining lease, giving only brief reasons based on that applicant’s experience, technical knowledge and history as a lessee.
The unsuccessful applicant challenged the decision in revision and submitted comments and rejoinders, including material not before the State Government.
The Central Government rejected the revision by stating that it found no valid ground to interfere, without setting out reasons or expressly adopting the State Government’s reasons.
The revision decision was subject to further challenge before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The Central Government was required to make a speaking order. Its unexplained rejection was set aside, and the revision applications were remitted for fresh decision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 30 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1957, and Rules 54 and 55 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, the Central Government exercises quasi-judicial revisional functions and considers the record, including comments and counter-comments from the parties. Rule 26 requires the State Government to give reasons when refusing a lease, but the absence of an express reasons requirement in Rule 55 does not remove the reviewing authority’s duty to explain its decision. Reasons are needed to disclose the authority’s reasoning, allow parties to understand the decision, and enable effective appellate or supervisory review under Articles 136 and 227. The Court followed Shivji Nathubhai v. Union of India, M.P. Industries v. Union, Harinagar Sugar Mills Ltd. v. Shyam Sundar Jhunjhunwala, and Sardar Govindrao v. State; it distinguished Nandram Hunatram, Calcutta v. Union of India and Commissioner of Income-tax v. K. V. Pilliah.

rule.if: revision_proceeding and quasi_judicial_adjudication and important_rights_determined and further_challenge_available and (fresh_material_submitted or original_reasons_inadequate) and no_reasoned_decision

predicates.revision_proceeding: An unsuccessful applicant sought revision of a decision granting a mining lease to another applicant.
predicates.quasi_judicial_adjudication: The reviewing authority resolved competing claims in a judicial or quasi-judicial capacity.
predicates.important_rights_determined: The decision determined important rights of the competing applicants.
predicates.further_challenge_available: The reviewing authority’s decision could be challenged before a higher court.
predicates.fresh_material_submitted: The parties submitted comments or counter-comments containing material not before the original decision-maker.
predicates.original_reasons_inadequate: The original decision-maker gave brief or unclear reasons for preferring one applicant over another.
predicates.no_reasoned_decision: The reviewing authority neither stated its own reasons nor expressly adopted adequate reasons given by the original decision-maker.

issues.definition: When a quasi-judicial revision determines important rights and may be challenged further, the reviewing authority must give reasons if fresh material was submitted or the original reasons were inadequate and the reviewing authority gives no reasoned decision.
